gloss: to be on the defensive; to fall behind

definitions.gloss: to be on the defensive; to fall behind; to be reactive rather than proactive
definitions.explanation: To end up in a position where one can only react to events rather than control them. Originally from shogi/go terminology where 後手 means the second player (who moves second). Implies a disadvantageous position.

examples.japanese: {対応|たいおう}が{後手|ごて}に{回|まわ}った。
{政府|せいふ}の{対策|たいさく}は{後手|ごて}に{回|まわ}っていると{批判|ひはん}された。
examples.english: The government's measures were criticized for being reactive.

examples.japanese: {競合|きょうごう}に{先|さき}を{越|こ}されて{後手|ごて}に{回|まわ}らないように、{早|はや}めに{新商品|しんしょうひん}を{投入|とうにゅう}すべきだ。
examples.english: We should launch the new product early so we don't fall behind our competitors.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
From board game terminology. In shogi and go, {後手|ごて} refers to the player who moves second, which is generally considered a disadvantage. {後手|ごて}に{回|まわ}る means to be put into that second-mover position.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {後手|ごて}に{回|まわ}る vs. {先手|せんて}を{打|う}つ: Opposite expressions. {先手|せんて}を{打|う}つ means to take the initiative, to make the first move — the proactive counterpart.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {対応|たいおう}が{後手|ごて}に{回|まわ}る (the response falls behind)
- {対策|たいさく}が{後手|ごて}に{回|まわ}る (measures are reactive)
- {後手|ごて}に{回|まわ}らないように (so as not to fall behind)

USAGE:
Very common in news and business contexts when criticizing slow or reactive responses to problems, especially by organizations and governments.
